Joan Westenberg.notes: Substack. Author migrated ghost.io -> beehiiv -> substack; email delivery stopped after 2026-06-06, so everything from 2026-08 onward is web-only. Mode is 'json' because the HTML archive is infinite-scroll: it server-renders only 12 posts and IGNORES ?offset= (verified: page 2 returns page 1, new_on_page_2=0). The /api/v1/archive endpoint paginates correctly.

sources.notes: Current publication, from 2026-07-20. Listed first so it is the primary source: if a post ever appears in both archives, this version wins. Mode is 'json' for the usual Substack reason — the HTML archive server-renders only ~9 entries (2 of which are the /podcast and /notes tabs, not posts) and the rest is client-rendered, so mode 'html' would silently backfill one page. 7 posts, returned in a single API page.

Still live and still serving its own archive: the rename to Resight did NOT carry the back catalogue to the new subdomain, which is why this label needs two sources. 23 posts, single API page. Its own sender is set so backfilled front matter carries the address these posts actually went out from.

Neel Chhabra.notes: One label, two Substack publications. Neel rebranded 'Neel’s Newsletter' (neelchhabra@substack.com) to 'Resight' (resight@substack.com) and moved to a new subdomain; email delivery gaps 2026-05-09 to 2026-08-22, and the archives did not merge. The sender-timeline query in the backfill-mapping skill is what surfaces this — two senders whose date ranges do not abut. See 'A rebrand can split one label across two archives' in LEARNINGS.md.
